claims: Issue #664 reports s(271) <= 16.948947733714, the exact rational side 16948947733713657510723401112423/1000000000000000000000000000000 of search/packer/candidates/s271_ex1.cert rounded up at 12 places, 4.46e-5 below Francisco Couzo's #561 (16.948992356451); it prints the SHA-256 of s271_ex1.cert and of s271_ex1_regularized.cert, the same packing at the same side regularized for display with 21 angle groups.

The issue calls it a refinement of the #561 packing, not a new construction, and a different local minimum: its load-bearing tilt angles match #561's group for group within 0.12 degrees, except that four squares near 31.7 to 32.0 degrees in #561 are three here; KKT, strict modulo 54 exact flat motions against #561's 56, no corner-corner MILP descent, 116 + 1488 contact equations, 259 corner-corner contacts and 4 rattlers; matched over the eight symmetries, 59 load-bearing squares move by more than 1e-4 and 2 by more than 1e-2. These are numerical evidence at 80 digits, as the issue says, not interval proofs.

The issue says the basin explorer (search/packer/explore.py) started from the register's witness for 271 as one of 52 counts in a test run, and the improvement came 90 seconds in from one move that swaps the tilt angles of two neighbouring squares, then a re-polish; exactsolve.py certified the point.

The author's two standard-library exact checkers, verify_cert.py (separating axes) and verify_cert2.py (polygon intersection), are reported to accept both files; they share an author and the certificate format. No closed form, interval proof of local optimality or optimality is claimed.
